answers.answer: Open Economy in the sidebar and choose the Store tab. Choose New item, and the New store item dialog opens. Type a name in Item name, type any short label in Effect kind (for example sound), then set Cost and the other fields from the table. Choose Save item. Viewers still cannot buy the item from the dashboard: the viewer store shows Coming soon, so an integration has to submit each purchase through the purchase endpoint.
answers.quote: Open Economy in the sidebar and choose the Store tab.

answers.answer: To add an item you need the Moderator, Lead moderator, Editor or Broadcaster role; the New item button shows only to those roles. Before purchases can work, two more things are needed: channel currency switched on with Currency on, and an integration that submits purchases for signed-in viewers. The first two paragraphs and 'What a purchase does' say this.
answers.quote: A Moderator, Lead moderator, Editor or Broadcaster may add, edit, switch and delete items.

answers.answer: After Save item, the dialog closes and the item shows in the list, switched on, with its cost under the name. A purchase that works takes the cost from the buyer's balance and sends no chat line of its own. A purchase that fails at any check charges nothing.
answers.quote: The dialog closes and the item shows in the list, switched on, with its cost under the name, such as “50 to buy”.

answers.answer: The new price does not change a purchase that was already submitted. The cost is taken from the buyer's balance when the purchase passes its checks, and the purchase is saved at that moment. A later refund credits the amount actually paid, not the new price. The new price applies only to purchases that come in after the edit.
answers.quote: When every check passes, the bot takes the cost from the buyer’s balance.

answers.answer: In step 5 you set Who can buy, but the warning that LeadModerator, Editor and Broadcaster do not restrict anyone comes after the table. A reader who picks Broadcaster at step 5 only learns later that the item is open to everyone. Step 5 does point to the table below, and the warning follows it directly, so the cost is a reread. Also, step 4 says to type any label, and only the table adds that Effect kind cannot change later.
answers.quote: Choosing LeadModerator, Editor or Broadcaster currently falls back to Everyone for the item’s role requirement; do not use those three choices to restrict purchases.

answers.answer: Read aloud, the raw API path with braces is hard to follow, and a dashboard user who is not writing an integration does not need it. The refund details (separate refund record, repeat refunds that credit again) are for integration authors and slow down a dashboard reader.
answers.quote: It does this by sending POST /api/v1/channels/{channelId}/economy/catalog/{itemId}/purchase, where {itemId} is the store item’s ID.

warning_review.reason: This is a reference page, and the 1272 words include the purchase checks, refund rules and the integration API path that the application case needs (what happens to a submitted purchase after a price edit). Each integrator section has its own heading, so a dashboard reader can skip it. No answer was blocked by the length, so the count alone is not a defect.

The 167 words before step 1 are the access rules (which roles may add items) and the Coming soon status, which says viewers cannot buy from the dashboard. Both are consequences that change what the steps do, so voice.md point 4 places them first. The purchase checks and refund detail come after the steps. The one permanent field, Effect kind, is flagged in the table before Save item, so the reader sees it before saving.
